sections.h2: Where is Union County, South Carolina?
sections.html:
Union County covers about 515 square miles in the upstate and is bordered by Cherokee, York, Chester, Fairfield, Newberry, Laurens and Spartanburg counties. Part of the Sumter National Forest lies inside it, and the Tyger River and Fairforest Creek are its major waterways (Wikipedia).

The county seat and largest community is the city of Union. U.S. 176 runs through the county, the Furman Fendley Highway is a four-lane connector to Spartanburg that began construction in 1984, and S.C. Highway 18 links Union and Jonesville.

The county was created in 1785 and named for the old Union Church, a shared log meetinghouse. Scots-Irish Presbyterian settlers had arrived in the mid-1700s near Fairforest Creek, and the county was divided between Loyalists and Patriots during the Revolution, with at least five battles fought in or near it, including Musgrove Mill, Fishdam Ford and Blackstock's Farm.

The old court town of Pinckneyville faded into a ghost town after its district was abolished in 1799. In 1897 the Draytonville and Gowdeysville townships were transferred to Cherokee County. In the 1930s the federal government bought poor-quality farmland, which became part of the Sumter National Forest.

An owner with very old family paper should ask a title company early whether the records sit where they expect.

sections.h2: What is the economy like in Union County?
sections.html:
Health care and social assistance is now the largest employment sector, at about 21.7% in the third quarter of 2023. County gross domestic product for 2022 was about $822.7 million.

Major employers include Milliken & Company, Sonoco, Walmart, Timken, Dollar General and the University of South Carolina Union. Textiles dominated the economy for much of the county's history, and the industry largely closed or moved overseas from the 1980s into the 1990s.

The city of Union counted 8,174 residents in 2020, down from a peak of 10,775 in 1970. Its median age is 42.0. Public schools are run by Union County Schools, and USC Union, a satellite campus, was founded in 1965.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Union's older neighborhoods?
sections.html:
Union has several historic districts listed on the National Register: the East Main Street-Douglass Heights Historic District, the South Street-South Church Street Historic District and the Union Downtown Historic District. If your house is inside one, ask the county about any local rules before exterior work.

Union has a humid subtropical climate. The Santuck weather station shows normal annual precipitation of about 44.6 inches and about 3 inches of snow, and the city's record high is 110 degrees with a record low of minus 11.

sections.h2: Which Union County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Four offices split the work, and the county's website lists a phone for each.

OfficeWhat it doesPhone
AssessorValues real property, about 22,000 parcels(864) 429-1650
AuditorTax bills, homestead exemptions, personal property(864) 429-1618
TreasurerTax payments(864) 429-1606
Delinquent Tax CollectorDelinquent taxes and the tax sale(864) 429-1617

The Assessor's office is at 203 West Main Street, Union, SC 29379, open Monday to Friday from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. excluding holidays. The Delinquent Tax Office is at the same street address and opens at 8:30 a.m. The main courthouse is at 210 W. Main Street. Manufacturing, railroad and utility property is valued by the SC Department of Revenue, not the county Assessor.

sections.h2: What did the 2025 reappraisal change in Union County?
sections.html:
The 2025 countywide reappraisal set an appraisal date of December 31, 2024, and the 2024 taxable value stays the same for the next four years, subject to listed exceptions. South Carolina law requires reappraisal every five years.

  • The notice of valuation and classification is not a tax bill.
  • The county must notify you of any change in value or classification of $1,000 or more.
  • Mill levies are set each year, so your bill can change even when the assessed value does not.
  • Not receiving a tax notice does not affect the validity of the tax, penalty, interest, due date or tax lien.

Keep your mailing address current with the Assessor in writing. Agricultural land that changes use is subject to rollback taxes for the current year and the three preceding years.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Union County assessment?
sections.html:
File an appeal within 90 days of the notice date to keep all of your options. Instructions are on the back of the valuation notice and on the Assessor's website.

An informal appeal form is available on the Assessor's page. The County Board of Assessment Appeals, appointed by County Council, holds conferences on classification and real property assessment and does not set values or taxes. Either the owner or the Assessor may contest its decision before the Administrative Law Judge Division, and either party may then appeal to the S.C. Supreme Court.

An appeal does not extend the payment deadline. Pay on time to avoid penalties and interest.

sections.h2: When is Union County property tax due?
sections.html:
Taxes are billed one year in arrears, notices go out each October and payment is due by January 15 without penalty. The Delinquent Tax Office page gives the schedule.

Payment datePenalty
After January 153%
After February 110%
After March 1615% plus execution costs

Taxes go delinquent on March 17, or the next business day. The county accepts cash, cashier's checks, postal money orders, certified checks and Visa or Mastercard in person, and also takes payment by mail, by phone and through a lockbox. It does not accept partial payments on delinquent bills because its system is not set up for them.

State law (S.C. Code 12-45-180) sets the same step-by-step penalty and gives the treasurer authority to waive penalties on clear and convincing evidence of timely payment.

sections.h2: What happens at the Union County tax sale?
sections.html:
Unpaid properties are sold at public sale, and a person who wants one must bid, because paying the taxes afterward does not transfer it. The annual sale was scheduled for November 10, 2026 at the Union County Elections Office, 1246 S Duncan By-Pass, with pre-registration from October 1. That date has passed as of this update, so call the Delinquent Tax Office at (864) 429-1617 for the result and any follow-up.

  • Delinquent properties are advertised in the Union County News for three consecutive weeks before the sale.
  • Properties that do not sell go to the Union County Forfeited Land Commission and are assigned first come, first served, in cash.
  • A property sold at tax sale can be redeemed with taxes, assessments, penalties and costs plus 3%, 6%, 9% or 12% interest.

The state code (12-51-90) sets a 12-month redemption window, and the county page does not state the length, so confirm it with the office.

sections.h2: What should you do before selling a Union County house with tax due?
sections.html:
• Ask the Treasurer or Delinquent Tax Collector for a written payoff with penalties.
  • Confirm the tax map number and the owner of record before closing.
  • If the notice went to a prior owner, ask about a waiver under state law.
  • Get a title search if the land is old family property.

We buy Union County houses as-is, including inherited homes and houses with unpaid taxes. Tell us the address and what you owe.

faqs.q: When are Union County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due by January 15 without penalty. The penalty is 3% after January 15, 10% after February 1 and 15% plus execution costs after March 16.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Union County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 90 days from the date of the notice. An appeal does not extend the payment deadline.

faqs.q: Does Union County accept partial payments on delinquent taxes?
faqs.a: No. The county says its bookkeeping system is not set up for partial payments.

faqs.q: Who do I call about Union County property tax?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor at (864) 429-1650 for values, the Auditor at (864) 429-1618 for tax bills and exemptions, the Treasurer at (864) 429-1606 for payments and the Delinquent Tax Collector at (864) 429-1617 for delinquent taxes.
